subject: NovaHealth security questionnaire: Hosted API data residency, retention and deletion
body:
From: Emily Carter <emily.carter@novahealth.com>

Cc: NovaHealth Security <security@novahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API questionnaire — residency & retention (spreadsheet attached)

Jonas —

Thanks for taking this. Attached is NovaHealth's standard security questionnaire focused on where customer data lives, how long it is retained, and the deletion workflow for hosted APIs. We have a few tight gates internally and need answers mapped to the spreadsheet rows (column "Vendor response") by end of week if possible. A few items we care about up front:

- Can customers restrict storage to US-only regions?
- How long are transient caches, request logs, and backups retained by default?
- What is the guaranteed window to fully purge a tenant’s data from all backups/replicas once deletion is requested?

Attached: security-questionnaire-novahealth.xlsx

Appreciate any pointers and a short summary doc (one pager) for our legal team.

Best,
Emily

Subject: Re: Hosted API questionnaire — residency & retention (spreadsheet attached)

Hi Emily —

Thanks for the questionnaire. We completed the vendor response column in the attached workbook and included a short executive summary (hostedapi-data-retention-summary.pdf). Below are the high-level responses called out for quick review; the spreadsheet has row-level mappings (Q1..Q46).

1) Region selection and geofencing
- Customers may choose primary storage region at tenant creation from available regions (US, EU, APAC).
- Backups and snapshots are, by default, stored in the same region as the tenant. Cross-region replication only occurs when explicit geo-redundancy is requested in the contract or by enabling multi-region failover.
- We do not provide a manual guarantee to block cross-region disaster recovery transfers outside of contractual geo-redundancy settings; please raise if NovaHealth requires legally-binding region-locking for backups.

2) Data types & default retention
- Transient in-memory caches (KV cache related to active sessions): ephemeral, retained for up to 2 hours by default; not persisted to disk.
- Request-level logs (request metadata and token counts, stripped of content hashes): default retention 30 days for troubleshooting and billing; can be shortened via support request for enterprise customers.
- Full request/response content: for hosted API, content retention is opt-in — default is not retained except when customer enables persistence for features like conversation history. If enabled, retention is configurable per-tenant (30/90/365 days typical presets).
- Backups and snapshots: primary storage snapshots are retained according to the tenant’s retention setting; automated point-in-time backups are retained for up to 30 days by default.

3) Deletion / purge procedure and timing
- Standard deletion workflow: customer submits tenant deletion request via Console or API -> deletion job removes tenant metadata and schedules secure wipe of object storage and KV entries -> background job removes snapshots and rotatable backups -> final attestation emailed to customer.
- Typical timeline: active metadata and user-facing data are removed within 24–72 hours post-request. Snapshots/backups and archived replicas are removed within 30 days.
- For strict purges (no cross-region copies, expedited wiping), we offer an expedited purge option (contract addendum) with a maximum window of 7 days for backup purge, subject to verification and additional cost.

4) Evidence and auditability
- We provide deletion attestation emails and can generate an audit bundle (log excerpts, job IDs, S3 object path removals) on request.
- All deletion operations are recorded in our audit logs (immutable, retained per account settings) and are available to customers via the Console and API.

5) Encryption and key management
- Data at rest is encrypted with AES-256. Customers may use Redwood-managed keys or BYOK (KMS/HSM integration) for enterprise/private deployments.
- Key rotation and revocation are supported; revoking a customer-managed key renders retained encrypted backups inaccessible.

Attachments: hostedapi-data-retention-summary.pdf, security-questionnaire-novahealth.xlsx (completed)

If NovaHealth requires more granular legal wording around region-lock guarantees or faster backup purge SLAs we can scope a short contract addendum.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Trust, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Emily — a couple of technical clarifications to support Kimberly's answers and to populate the spreadsheet cells Q14-Q18:

- KV / prefix caches: These are in-memory on serving nodes and are not persisted to object storage. TTL default = 2 hours; cache entries are evicted on node restart. No long-term persistence unless customer explicitly enables conversation history.

- Deletion API example (tenant-level):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/delete \\n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n    -d '{"expedite":false}'

  If "expedite":true and contracted, background purge priority increases and backup retention window is reduced per the addendum.

- Backups & snapshots: We retain automated snapshots for 30 days by default; deep cold archives (long-term backups) are only used if specifically enabled. When a tenant is deleted we enqueue removal of snapshots and confirm object deletions in storage; object paths and deletion job ids are included in the attestation bundle.

- Data used for model improvement: Redwood does not use customer prompt/response content for model training without explicit customer opt-in. Aggregated telemetry and usage metrics are used by default for product improvement (non-content).

- Evidence links: once deletion is processed we can provide a Drive link with the audit bundle (sample provided in attached summary).

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if your security team wants to review the workbook row-by-row.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Product Manager, Inference Platform
priyom.das@redwood.com
